phys-astro-01-c2.text: David Weinberg, Ohio State University Department of Astronomy. Lecture 8: Principles of Stellar Structure III. Nuclear Energy. Ohio State University Astronomy.
phys-astro-01-c2.quote: The mass of a helium nucleus is 6.643x10-24 g, 0.7% lighter.
phys-astro-01-c2.claim: The mass deficit is ~0.7% of the original hydrogen mass

phys-astro-01-c2.text: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Imagine the Universe. Life Cycles of Stars (X-ray spectra lesson background). NASA Imagine the Universe.
phys-astro-01-c2.quote: Creating heavier elements through fusing of iron thus requires an input of energy rather than the release of energy.
phys-astro-01-c2.claim: Iron is the most stable nucleus, so fusion beyond iron costs energy rather than releasing it.

phys-astro-01-c1.text: Britannica Editors (1998). Hertzsprung-Russell diagram. Encyclopedia Britannica.
phys-astro-01-c1.quote: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, in astronomy, graph in which the absolute magnitudes (intrinsic brightness) of stars are plotted against their spectral types (temperatures).
phys-astro-01-c1.claim: If you plot stellar luminosity (brightness) against surface temperature, you get the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram.

phys-astro-01-c1.text: NASA Science. Types of Stars. NASA Science.
phys-astro-01-c1.quote: Red dwarfs make up around 75% of the Milky Way galaxy's stellar population.
phys-astro-01-c1.claim: most stars are small red dwarfs

phys-astro-04-c1.text: Adam Riess (2009). Dark energy. Encyclopedia Britannica.
phys-astro-04-c1.quote: Dark energy was discovered in 1998 with this method by two international teams that included American astronomers Adam Riess (the author of this article) and Saul Perlmutter and Australian astronomer Brian Schmidt.
phys-astro-04-c1.claim: In 1998, two independent teams (led by Perlmutter, and by Schmidt and Riess) used Type Ia supernovae as 'standard candles' to measure cosmic distances.
